summary_plain: This investigation burned large composite fabric samples inside an expendable resupply vehicle after it left the International Space Station to study how fires grow in microgravity. Understanding large-scale fire behavior helps researchers improve material selection and fire safety for future crewed spacecraft. These experiments also provide insights that benefit fire safety and prevention in enclosed spaces on Earth.
summary_expert: SAFFIRE-I performed 2 tests using solid SIBAL fuels in the form of a sheet measuring 40.6 x 94 cm. The tests were conducted with oxygen levels ranging from 21.5 to 21.7 percent (mole fraction 0.21 to 0.22) and a forced air flow speed (ventilation velocity) of 20 cm/s, while flow direction was varied between tests. The objectives were to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate low-g flammability limits compared to normal gravity screening tests.

key_findings.text: The Saffire-I experiment provides a new way to study a realistic fire on an exploration vehicle by using an unmanned cargo vessel to measure oxygen, carbon dioxide, heat, pressure, flame growth, and capture video.
